pyruvic-acid-peel.text: Users book pyruvic acid peels to clear active acne and refresh dull, congested skin. It is a keratolytic peel described mainly for acne vulgaris, and the evidence for that use is a handful of small studies.

chain: Deep peel removes damaged skin layers
phenol-croton-oil-peel.text: The phenol-croton oil peel is the classic deep resurfacing treatment for wrinkles and skin tightening, with the smoother, tighter result visible once healing is complete. It has been used since the 1962 Baker-Gordon formula, and gentler low-phenol versions are now used as well.

chain: Strong TCA placed in scar base
Scar floor rebuilds with new collagen
chemical-reconstruction-of-skin-scars.text: People with ice-pick and other atrophic acne scars use CROSS to make individual scars shallower without treating the whole face. It has been studied in small trials for exactly this use.

skinvive.text: Skinvive is promoted for a hydrated, glassy glow and smoother texture rather than added volume. Users choose it as a skin-quality treatment, and the evidence for that use is early-stage.

chain: HA placed in superficial fat compartments
profhilo-structura.text: Profhilo Structura is marketed to restore cheek and facial volume, particularly in the lateral cheek, using a hybrid hyaluronic acid. People use it for a fuller, lifted midface, and the evidence for that use so far is small case series.

chain: Hybrid HA injected into body skin
profhilo-body.text: Profhilo Body is used to improve laxity and roughness of body skin such as the upper inner arms and backs of the hands. The evidence for that use is small single-arm trials.

rejuran-hb.text: Rejuran HB is a polynucleotide skin booster used in aesthetic clinics to improve skin quality and texture. Published human data for this specific product are very limited.

juvelook.text: Juvelook is a Korean PDLLA and hyaluronic acid biostimulator injected for tear troughs, folds and overall skin texture. Support comes from small studies and case reports.

lenisna.text: Lenisna is a PDLLA injectable used as a skin booster and collagen stimulator. Efficacy data for it are almost absent, and the main literature is a 2026 consensus on injection safety.

aesthefill.text: AestheFill is a Korean PDLLA microsphere biostimulator used to firm skin and soften lines gradually through collagen stimulation. Evidence includes one randomised trial against hyaluronic acid and many technique papers.

pure-polynucleotide-pdrn.text: PDRN is an injectable salmon-derived skin booster borrowed from wound-care medicine and promoted for skin quality, scars and aging signs. Lab and orthopaedic data are promising, while controlled evidence for facial appearance is limited.

volite-volift.text: Juvéderm Volite (VYC-12, also sold as Skinvive) is injected into the skin for smoothness and hydration rather than volume. Trials exist, mostly single-arm and manufacturer-linked.

restylane-vital-skinboosters.text: Restylane Vital is the longest-studied skin booster, used for elasticity and texture. Evidence for this use comes mostly from small clinical studies.

chain: HA gel fills lines and hollows
redensity.text: Teoxane's Redensity hyaluronic acid products are used for fine lines and under-eye hollows, with the smoothing visible after the gel is placed. Evidence includes a randomised 52-week perioral trial.

sunekos.text: Sunekos is an Italian biorevitalising booster used for photoaged face skin, the eye area and lax skin on thighs, knees and arms. Support is mainly small manufacturer-linked trials.

exosome-facial.text: Exosome facials are used after microneedling or laser to improve skin quality, texture and scarring. Evidence for the appearance use is small early studies, and no exosome product is FDA-approved.

chain: Skin receives HA, vitamins or PRP
mesogun.text: A mesogun delivers mesotherapy solutions such as hyaluronic acid, vitamins or PRP across the face for glow and hydration. Evidence specific to the device is sparse.

prp-platelet-rich-plasma-injections.text: PRP is used for skin rejuvenation, wrinkles, under-eye areas and hair, and is often paired with microneedling as a vampire facial. Trial evidence is mostly from knees rather than faces.

chain: Own fibrin clot placed under eyes
Lighter dark circles, fuller eye area
prf-platelet-rich-fibrin.text: Forum users try PRF for dark under-eye circles and eye bags, and some report mixed results. It is established in dental surgery, and no facial trials were found.

chain: Fillers placed in several face areas
liquid-facelift.text: A liquid facelift is the marketing term for combining fillers, often hyaluronic acid, in one session to restore volume and contour without surgery, with the change visible immediately. The literature is mostly reviews.

collagen-induction-therapy.text: Microneedling or dermarolling is used for acne scars, wrinkles and texture, and is often combined with PRP or topicals. Scars are the best-studied use, with more modest evidence for wrinkles and texture.

aqualyx.text: Aqualyx is a deoxycholate injectable sold in Europe for localized fat, and forum users discuss it for facial hollowing and slimming. That facial use goes beyond clinical evidence, and claims of permanence are anecdotal.

follicular-unit-extraction-fue.text: FUE is a hair transplant method that restores density to receding or thinning areas and avoids a linear donor scar. The restored hair is visible once grafts grow in, at the cost of longer surgery.

chain: Scalp strip taken from donor area
follicular-unit-transplantation-fut.text: FUT, or strip harvesting, is a hair transplant technique that moves donor hair to thinning areas, producing visible new density and leaving a thin linear donor scar. It is the older of the two main harvest methods.

direct-hair-implantation-dhi.text: DHI is an FUE variant using an implanter pen, promoted by clinics for precise placement and density. The transplanted hair is visibly restored, while independent comparisons with other methods are scarce.

sapphire-fue.text: Sapphire FUE is promoted as giving finer incisions, denser placement and faster healing for hair transplants. The hair restoration itself is visible, while independent evidence for the sapphire-blade advantage is limited.

chain: Pen makes incision and places graft
choi-implanter-pen.text: The Choi implanter pen is the tool behind DHI, used to place follicular units in a single step during hair transplants. Clinics promote its precision, and published comparisons are absent.

chain: Bald scalp skin is cut out
scalp-reduction.text: Scalp reduction removes a segment of hairless scalp so surrounding hair covers more of the head, shrinking the bald area visibly. It is an older adjunct to hair transplantation, with sparse modern evidence.

chain: Grafts are transplanted to thin areas
artas-robotic-system.text: ARTAS is an FDA-cleared image-guided robot that automates donor hair extraction in FUE transplants, which restore visible density. Published outcome data were thin in the sources.

chain: Grafts are implanted in thin areas
neograft.text: NeoGraft is an automated suction-assisted FUE device reported as FDA-approved in 2009, used to harvest and deliver grafts for hair transplants. Little outcome data has been published.
